records.source: מִי־זֶ֣ה׀בָּ֣א מֵאֱד֗וֹם חֲמ֤וּץ בְּגָדִים֙ מִבָּצְרָ֔ה זֶ֚ה הָד֣וּר בִּלְבוּשׁ֔וֹ צֹעֶ֖ה בְּרֹ֣ב כֹּח֑וֹ אֲנִ֛י מְדַבֵּ֥ר בִּצְדָקָ֖ה רַ֥ב לְהוֹשִֽׁיעַ׃
records.gloss: Who [is] this coming from Edom, red of garments from Bozrah, this [one] splendid in his clothing, bending in [the] greatness of his strength? I, speaking in righteousness, great to save.
pieces: Who is this arriving from Edom, coming from Bozrah with clothing dyed red, \q so majestic in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} robes, \q pressing on in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} immense strength? \q It is I, who speak in righteousness, with great power to save.

L.1: Who [is] this coming from Edom, [with] garments stained red, from Bozrah, \q this [one] splendid in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} clothing, \q striding in the greatness of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} strength? \q I, speaking in righteousness, mighty to save.

R.1: Who is this coming from the land of Edom, from the city of Bozrah? His clothes are bright red. \q He is dressed in splendid clothes, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} marches forward with great strength. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answers: It is I. I speak what is right, and I have great power to save.

decisions.choice: the one coming is the LORD as a warrior, returning from judging his enemies
decisions.reason: He answers in the first person with God's own claims (righteousness, power to save), and verse 5 repeats 59:16, where the LORD sees there is no one to help and his own arm saves. Revelation 19:13-15 draws on this passage for the rider whose robe is dipped in blood and who treads the winepress.

decisions.choice: Edom and Bozrah: Israel's hostile neighbor and its chief city, standing for the nations opposed to God's people
decisions.reason: Edom, descended from Esau, was a bitter enemy of Judah (Psalm 137:7; Obadiah 10-14). Isaiah 34:5-6 already pictures God's sword on Edom and a slaughter in Bozrah. The name Edom sounds like the word for red (verse 2), and Bozrah sounds like the word for grape harvest.

decisions.choice: striding: moving forward in strength
decisions.reason: The received text has a verb that elsewhere means to stoop or bend (51:14), perhaps of a man leaning forward as he marches. With one letter different the verb means to march (Judges 5:4; Psalm 68:8). Either way, he comes on in great strength.

decisions.choice: the land of Edom, the city of Bozrah; The LORD answers
decisions.reason: Readable says what Edom and Bozrah are and names the speaker who answers, following the meaning decision on who is coming.

records.heading: The one coming from Edom

records.source: מַדּ֥וּעַ אָדֹ֖ם לִלְבוּשֶׁ֑ךָ וּבְגָדֶ֖יךָ כְּדֹרֵ֥ךְ בְּגַֽת׃
records.gloss: Why [is there] red to your clothing, and your garments like [one] treading in a winepress?
pieces: Why are {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} robes so red? \q Why do {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} clothes look like those of a man stamping grapes in a winepress?

L.2: Why [is] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} clothing red, \q and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} garments like [one] treading in a winepress?

R.2: Why are {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} clothes red? \q They look like the clothes of someone who has been stomping on grapes to make wine.

decisions.choice: treading in a winepress: crushing grapes by foot in a stone vat, a picture of judgment
decisions.reason: Grapes were trampled in a vat cut in rock, and the juice splashed the treaders' clothes. The image is used for God's judgment in Lamentations 1:15, Joel 4:13 and Revelation 14:19-20; 19:15.

decisions.choice: red: the color of the stains; the word sounds like Edom
decisions.reason: The question picks up "Edom" from verse 1 by sound: the one from Edom is red.

decisions.choice: to make wine
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a winepress is for.

records.source: פּוּרָ֣ה׀דָּרַ֣כְתִּי לְבַדִּ֗י וּמֵֽעַמִּים֙ אֵֽין־אִ֣ישׁ אִתִּ֔י וְאֶדְרְכֵ֣ם בְּאַפִּ֔י וְאֶרְמְסֵ֖ם בַּחֲמָתִ֑י וְיֵ֤ז נִצְחָם֙ עַל־בְּגָדַ֔י וְכָל־מַלְבּוּשַׁ֖י אֶגְאָֽלְתִּי׃
records.gloss: [The] winepress I have trodden by myself, and from [the] peoples there was no one with me; and I trod them in my anger, and I trampled them in my rage; and spattered their juice on my garments, and all my clothes I have stained.
pieces: Alone I have trampled the grapes in the press; from the peoples no one joined {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q In {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger I stamped on them; \q in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} fury I crushed them underfoot. \q Their juice splashed across {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} garments, \q and every piece of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} clothing is stained.

L.3: The winepress I have trodden alone, and from the peoples there was no one with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; \q and I trod them in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger, \q and I trampled them in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath, \q and their juice spattered on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} garments, \q and I have stained all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} clothing.

R.3: I have stomped the grapes in the winepress all alone. No one from the nations came to help {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q I was angry, so I stomped on the nations. I crushed them in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} great anger. \q Their blood splashed on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} clothes and stained all of them.

decisions.choice: their juice: the juice of the grapes in the picture, standing for the blood of the peoples
decisions.reason: The word is used of the juice of grapes and of lifeblood. Verse 6 shows the grapes are the peoples.

decisions.choice: alone, with no one with me: God carries out judgment and rescue by himself
decisions.reason: No human ally shares the work; the same point is made in 59:16 and 63:5. God alone saves his people and judges their enemies.

decisions.choice: I trod, I trampled: told as a deed already done
decisions.reason: The warrior reports what he has just done. Several of the verb forms could also be read as future ("I will tread them"), which would make this a judgment still to come.

decisions.choice: stomped on the nations; their blood
decisions.reason: Readable says what the grapes and their juice stand for, following the meaning decision.

records.source: כִּ֛י י֥וֹם נָקָ֖ם בְּלִבִּ֑י וּשְׁנַ֥ת גְּאוּלַ֖י בָּֽאָה׃
records.gloss: For a day of vengeance [was] in my heart, and [the] year of my redeemed [ones] had come.
pieces: For I had set {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heart on a day of vengeance, \q and the year for redeeming {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own had come.

L.4: For a day of vengeance [was] in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heart, \q and the year of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} redeemed had come.

R.4: I had decided that it was time to punish {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} enemies. \q The year had come for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to rescue {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people.

decisions.choice: a day of vengeance and a year: the time God has set for judgment and rescue
decisions.reason: The pair appears in 34:8 and 61:2, where the anointed one proclaims the year of the LORD's favor and the day of vengeance of our God. The short day of judgment stands beside the longer year of rescue.

decisions.choice: my redeemed: the people God redeems; the time to redeem them
decisions.reason: The form is a plural noun that can mean "my redeemed ones" or "my redemption". Either way it is the time when God buys back his people.

decisions.choice: vengeance: just punishment by the rightful judge
decisions.reason: It is not personal spite but God setting wrongs right and defending his people (Deuteronomy 32:35, 41-43; 35:4).

decisions.choice: punish my enemies; rescue my people
decisions.reason: Readable says who is punished and who is rescued.

records.source: וְאַבִּיט֙ וְאֵ֣ין עֹזֵ֔ר וְאֶשְׁתּוֹמֵ֖ם וְאֵ֣ין סוֹמֵ֑ךְ וַתּ֤וֹשַֽׁע לִי֙ זְרֹעִ֔י וַחֲמָתִ֖י הִ֥יא סְמָכָֽתְנִי׃
records.gloss: And I looked, and there was no helper, and I was appalled, and there was no supporter; and gave victory to me my arm, and my rage, it upheld me.
pieces: I looked around, and there was no one to help; \q I stared, dismayed, and no one came to support. \q So {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own arm brought {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} victory, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} fury kept {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} going.

L.5: And I looked, and there was no helper, \q and I was appalled, and there was no one upholding; \q so {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} arm gave victory to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath, it upheld {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

R.5: I looked for someone to help {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, but there was no one. \q I was shocked that no one came to stand with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q So I used {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own power to win the battle. \q My anger kept {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} strong.

decisions.choice: no one to help, my arm saved: almost the words of 59:16
decisions.reason: In 59:16 the LORD saw there was no one to step in, and his own arm brought salvation. The warrior of 63:1-6 is the same LORD doing what that verse describes.

decisions.choice: my arm: my own power
decisions.reason: The arm stands for strength in action (40:10; 52:10; 62:8).

decisions.choice: gave victory: the verb usually rendered save, here of winning the battle
decisions.reason: Saving in this passage is rescue by defeating the enemy; the verb is the same as in verse 1, "mighty to save".

decisions.choice: victory, win the battle
decisions.reason: The setting is a battle, so the verb is put as winning it, rather than with "save"; the meaning decision explains the link.

records.source: וְאָב֤וּס עַמִּים֙ בְּאַפִּ֔י וַאֲשַׁכְּרֵ֖ם בַּחֲמָתִ֑י וְאוֹרִ֥יד לָאָ֖רֶץ נִצְחָֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And I trampled peoples in my anger, and I made them drunk in my rage, and I brought down to the ground their juice.
pieces: I crushed peoples underfoot in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger; \q I made them drunk on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} fury, \q and I let their lifeblood run down to the earth.

L.6: And I trampled peoples in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger, \q and I made them drunk in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath, \q and I brought down their juice to the earth.

R.6: I was angry, and I stomped on the nations. \q I made them drink {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger until they staggered like drunk people. \q I poured out their blood on the ground.

decisions.choice: made them drunk: made them drink the cup of God's wrath
decisions.reason: Judgment is pictured as a cup of wine that makes the drinker stagger and fall (51:17-23; Jeremiah 25:15-16).

decisions.choice: made them drunk: the received text
decisions.reason: Some Hebrew manuscripts read "I shattered them", a word that differs by one letter. The received text keeps the wine picture of verses 2-3.

decisions.choice: their juice: their lifeblood
decisions.reason: The same word as in verse 3; the picture of grapes gives way to its meaning.

decisions.choice: made them drink my anger until they staggered like drunk people
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the cup of wrath.

records.source: חַֽסְדֵ֨י יְהוָ֤ה׀אַזְכִּיר֙ תְּהִלֹּ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה כְּעַ֕ל כֹּ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־גְּמָלָ֖נוּ יְהוָ֑ה וְרַב־טוּב֙ לְבֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁר־גְּמָלָ֥ם כְּֽרַחֲמָ֖יו וּכְרֹ֥ב חֲסָדָֽיו׃
records.gloss: [The] loyal loves of Yahweh I will cause to be remembered, [the] praises of Yahweh, according to all that Yahweh has dealt out to us, and [the] great goodness to [the] house of Israel which he has dealt out to them according to his compassions and according to [the] abundance of his loyal loves.
pieces: I will bring to mind the acts of loyal love {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has shown, \q the deeds that make {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} worthy of praise, \q for all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has done for us: \q the great goodness {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has shown to the house of Israel, \q out of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} tender mercy and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} abundant loyal love.

L.7: I will recount the [acts of] loyal love of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the praises of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q according to all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has done for us, \q and the great goodness to the house of Israel \q which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done for them according to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} compassion and according to the abundance of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love.

R.7: I will tell about the faithful love of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q I will praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for everything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done for us. \q He has been very good to the people of Israel. \q He has been kind to them because {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithful love is so great.

decisions.choice: loyal love (plural): the acts in which God's loyal love was shown
decisions.reason: The plural points to concrete deeds of covenant faithfulness, which verses 8-14 go on to recall: the exodus, the sea, the wilderness (Psalm 89:2; Lamentations 3:22).

decisions.choice: I will recount: literally "I will cause to be remembered", spoken aloud before God
decisions.reason: It is the same verb as "you who remind the LORD" in 62:6. The prayer that follows (63:7-64:11) is such a reminder: it recalls what God has done and asks him to act again.

decisions.choice: compassion: tender, deep pity
decisions.reason: The word is related to the word for womb and is used of a mother's love for her child (49:15).

decisions.choice: I will praise him
decisions.reason: Readable puts "the praises of the LORD" (the deeds for which he is praised) as an act of praising him.

records.heading: Remembering the loyal love of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אַךְ־עַמִּ֣י הֵ֔מָּה בָּנִ֖ים לֹ֣א יְשַׁקֵּ֑רוּ וַיְהִ֥י לָהֶ֖ם לְמוֹשִֽׁיעַ׃
records.gloss: And he said, Surely my people they [are], children [who] will not deal falsely; and he became to them a savior.
pieces: He said, "Without doubt they are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, \q children who will not be false to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}." \q So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} became the one who saved them.

L.8: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Surely they [are] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, \q children [who] will not deal falsely"; \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} became a savior to them.

R.8: He said, "They really are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people. \q They are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} children, and they will not lie to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} or turn against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}." \q So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} became the one who saved them.

decisions.choice: deal falsely: break faith, be disloyal
decisions.reason: The verb is used of breaking a covenant or promise (Psalm 44:18; 89:34). God chose Israel trusting that they would be loyal; verse 10 tells how they rebelled.

decisions.choice: children: Israel as God's children
decisions.reason: Israel is God's son and his children in 1:2, Exodus 4:22 and Deuteronomy 14:1. The thought prepares for "you are our Father" in verse 16.

decisions.choice: savior: the one who rescues them
decisions.reason: Isaiah calls the LORD Israel's savior again and again (43:3, 11; 45:15, 21; 49:26; 60:16).

decisions.choice: be false to me; lie to me or turn against me
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whom they would be false to; Readable gives the two sides of the verb, speaking falsely and breaking faith.

records.source: בְּֽכָל־צָרָתָ֣ם׀ל֣וֹ צָ֗ר וּמַלְאַ֤ךְ פָּנָיו֙ הֽוֹשִׁיעָ֔ם בְּאַהֲבָת֥וֹ וּבְחֶמְלָת֖וֹ ה֣וּא גְאָלָ֑ם וַֽיְנַטְּלֵ֥ם וַֽיְנַשְּׂאֵ֖ם כָּל־יְמֵ֥י עוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: In all their distress to him [there was] distress, and [the] angel of his presence saved them; in his love and in his pity he redeemed them, and he lifted them up and he carried them all [the] days of old.
pieces: Whenever they were in trouble, it troubled {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and the angel of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence rescued them. \q In {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} love and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} pity {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} redeemed them; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} picked them up and carried them throughout the ages long past.

L.9: In all their distress, to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} [there was] distress, and the angel of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence saved them; \q in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} love and in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} pity {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} redeemed them, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lifted them up and carried them all the days of old.

R.9: When they suffered, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} suffered with them, and the angel of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence saved them. \q Because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loved them and felt sorry for them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} bought them back. \q He picked them up and carried them all through the years long ago.

decisions.choice: to him there was distress: the reading tradition (qere), "he was distressed"
alternatives: not an envoy or an angel, but his presence saved them
decisions.reason: The written text (ketiv) has "not" where the reading tradition has "to him"; the two words sound alike. The written text would give "in all their distress he was not an enemy" or "it was no distress". The Septuagint, dividing and voicing the words differently, reads "not an envoy or an angel, but he himself saved them". The reading tradition, followed here, says God shared his people's suffering (Judges 10:16).

decisions.choice: the angel of his presence: the angel in whom God himself went with his people
decisions.reason: At the exodus God sent his angel before Israel, with his own name in him (Exodus 23:20-23), and promised, "My presence will go with you" (Exodus 33:14-15). The word for presence is literally "face".

decisions.choice: lifted them up and carried them: as a parent carries a child
decisions.reason: The same picture is in 46:3-4, Deuteronomy 1:31 and Exodus 19:4.

records.source: וְהֵ֛מָּה מָר֥וּ וְעִצְּב֖וּ אֶת־ר֣וּחַ קָדְשׁ֑וֹ וַיֵּהָפֵ֥ךְ לָהֶ֛ם לְאוֹיֵ֖ב ה֥וּא נִלְחַם־בָּֽם׃
records.gloss: But they, they rebelled and grieved [the] spirit of his holiness; and he turned himself to them into an enemy; he, he fought against them.
pieces: But they rebelled and caused {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Holy Spirit grief, \q so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} changed into their enemy and went to war against them {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}.

L.10: But they rebelled and grieved {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Holy Spirit; \q so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} turned to become their enemy; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} fought against them.

R.10: But they turned against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They made {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Holy Spirit sad. \q So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} became their enemy, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} fought against them.

decisions.choice: grieved his Holy Spirit: God's own Spirit, present among his people, can be grieved
decisions.reason: Literally "the spirit of his holiness"; the phrase is found in the Old Testament only here, in verse 11 and in Psalm 51:13. The Spirit is spoken of as one who can be hurt, as God himself is (Psalm 78:40). Ephesians 4:30 takes up the words: "do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God".

decisions.choice: they rebelled: Israel's rebellion in the wilderness
decisions.reason: Psalm 78:40 and 106:33, 43 describe the same rebellion after the exodus, and Numbers 14 tells it.

decisions.choice: he turned into their enemy: God himself fought against his people
decisions.reason: Their Savior (verse 8) became their opponent, as in Lamentations 2:5, "the Lord has become like an enemy".

decisions.choice: Holy Spirit, with capital letters
decisions.reason: The Spirit is God's own Spirit, so it is written with a capital S, and "of his holiness" is put as "Holy"; compare Ephesians 4:30.

records.source: וַיִּזְכֹּ֥ר יְמֵֽי־עוֹלָ֖ם מֹשֶׁ֣ה עַמּ֑וֹ אַיֵּ֣ה׀הַֽמַּעֲלֵ֣ם מִיָּ֗ם אֵ֚ת רֹעֵ֣י צֹאנ֔וֹ אַיֵּ֛ה הַשָּׂ֥ם בְּקִרְבּ֖וֹ אֶת־ר֥וּחַ קָדְשֽׁוֹ׃
records.gloss: And he remembered [the] days of old, Moses, his people: Where [is] the [one who] brought them up from the sea with [the] shepherds of his flock? Where [is] the [one who] put in its midst [the] spirit of his holiness,
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people thought back to ancient times, to the days of Moses: \q "Where is the one who brought them, with the shepherds of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} flock, up out of the sea? \q Where is the one who put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Holy Spirit in their midst,

L.11: Then [one] remembered the days of old, Moses, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people: \q "Where [is] the [one who] brought them up from the sea with the shepherds of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} flock? \q Where [is] the [one who] put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Holy Spirit in its midst,

R.11: Then {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people remembered what happened long ago, in the time of Moses. \q They asked, "Where is the God who brought them up out of the sea, along with the leaders who cared for them like shepherds? \q Where is the God who put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Holy Spirit among them?

decisions.choice: he remembered: his people remembered, and asked where God had gone
alternatives: God remembered the days of old
decisions.reason: The verb is singular, and "his people" can be its subject (a people spoken of as one). The questions that follow look for God, so they are the people's words. The subject could instead be God, who remembered the old days; then the questions are his. The Hebrew does not say.

decisions.choice: the shepherds of his flock: the received text (plural), Moses and Aaron
decisions.reason: Psalm 77:21 says God led his people like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron, and Micah 6:4 names Moses, Aaron and Miriam. Some manuscripts and the Septuagint have the singular "shepherd", meaning Moses; Hebrews 13:20 seems to echo that form.

decisions.choice: put his Holy Spirit among them: God's Spirit with Israel in the wilderness
decisions.reason: God put his Spirit on the seventy elders (Numbers 11:17, 25), and Haggai 2:5 recalls that his Spirit stood among them when they came out of Egypt. Nehemiah 9:20 speaks of his good Spirit given to teach them.

decisions.choice: his people thought back, to the days of Moses; They asked
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the subject chosen in the meaning decision and introduce the questions as the people's words.

decisions.choice: the God who brought them up; the leaders who cared for them like shepherds
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one asked about and explains the shepherds as leaders.

records.source: מוֹלִיךְ֙ לִימִ֣ין מֹשֶׁ֔ה זְר֖וֹעַ תִּפְאַרְתּ֑וֹ בּ֤וֹקֵֽעַ מַ֨יִם֙ מִפְּנֵיהֶ֔ם לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת ל֖וֹ שֵׁ֥ם עוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: [who] caused to go at [the] right hand of Moses [the] arm of his splendor, [who] split [the] waters before them to make for himself a name of perpetuity,
pieces: who made {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glorious arm march at Moses' right side, \q who split the waters in front of them \q to win {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} a name that lasts forever,

L.12: [who] caused {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} splendid arm to go at the right hand of Moses, \q [who] split the waters before them \q to make for {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} an everlasting name,

R.12: He sent {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glorious power to go along with Moses. \q He split the sea in two in front of them. \q He did it to make {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name famous forever.

decisions.choice: his glorious arm at Moses' right hand: God's power working alongside Moses
decisions.reason: When Moses stretched out his hand and staff, God's power did the work (Exodus 14:16, 21; 17:11). The arm stands for that power (verse 5).

decisions.choice: split the waters: the crossing of the sea at the exodus
decisions.reason: Exodus 14:21; Psalm 78:13; Nehemiah 9:11. The same verb is used in those passages.

decisions.choice: an everlasting name: a reputation that lasts forever
decisions.reason: God's deeds at the exodus made his name known among the nations (Exodus 9:16; Nehemiah 9:10; 55:13).

decisions.choice: He sent ... He split ...
decisions.reason: Readable turns the chain of descriptions after "Where is the God who" into short statements about him; the questions of verse 11 still govern them.

records.source: מוֹלִיכָ֖ם בַּתְּהֹמ֑וֹת כַּסּ֥וּס בַּמִּדְבָּ֖ר לֹ֥א יִכָּשֵֽׁלוּ׃
records.gloss: [who] caused them to walk through the depths? Like a horse in the wilderness, not they stumbled.
pieces: who guided them through the depths, \q so that they did not stumble, sure-footed as a horse on the open plain?"

L.13: [who] led them through the depths? \q Like a horse in the wilderness, they did not stumble."

R.13: He led them through the deep water. \q They did not trip or fall. They were like a horse running easily across a desert plain."

decisions.choice: the depths: the deep waters of the sea at the exodus
decisions.reason: The same word is used for the sea Israel crossed in 51:10 and Exodus 15:5, 8.

decisions.choice: like a horse in the wilderness: sure-footed, on easy ground
decisions.reason: The wilderness here is open grazing land, where a horse runs without tripping. The sea bed was as easy as open ground (Psalm 106:9, "through the deep as through a wilderness").

decisions.choice: so that they did not stumble, sure-footed as a horse
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the line inside the question and puts the comparison last, where it explains the stumbling.

records.source: כַּבְּהֵמָה֙ בַּבִּקְעָ֣ה תֵרֵ֔ד ר֥וּחַ יְהוָ֖ה תְּנִיחֶ֑נּוּ כֵּ֚ן נִהַ֣גְתָּ עַמְּךָ֔ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת לְךָ֖ שֵׁ֥ם תִּפְאָֽרֶת׃
records.gloss: Like livestock [that] into the valley goes down, [the] spirit of Yahweh gave him rest. So you led your people to make for yourself a name of splendor.
pieces: As cattle make their way down into a valley, \q the Spirit of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} brought them to rest. \q In this way {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} guided {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, to make for {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} a name full of splendor.

L.14: Like livestock [that] go down into the valley, \q the Spirit of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave them rest. \q So {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} led {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, to make for {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} a name of splendor.

R.14: The Spirit of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} led them to a place of rest, the way cattle walk down into a valley to rest. \q That is how {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} led {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people. \q You did it so that {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name would be honored and praised.

decisions.choice: gave them rest: the received text
decisions.reason: The Septuagint and some other ancient versions have "guided them", a verb that differs by one letter and matches "you led" in the next line. The received text speaks of the rest God gave Israel in the land (Deuteronomy 12:9-10; Joshua 21:44).

decisions.choice: livestock going down into the valley: to water and pasture at the end of the day
decisions.reason: Herds were driven down from the dry hills to the valley floor, where there was water and grass. The picture is of Israel brought safely to rest.

decisions.choice: you led your people: the prayer now speaks to God directly
decisions.reason: From here to 64:11 the prayer addresses God as "you".

decisions.choice: The Spirit of the LORD led them to a place of rest, the way cattle walk down into a valley
decisions.reason: Readable puts the main statement first and the comparison second.

records.source: הַבֵּ֤ט מִשָּׁמַ֨יִם֙ וּרְאֵ֔ה מִזְּבֻ֥ל קָדְשְׁךָ֖ וְתִפְאַרְתֶּ֑ךָ אַיֵּ֤ה קִנְאָֽתְךָ֙ וּגְב֣וּרֹתֶ֔ךָ הֲמ֥וֹן מֵעֶ֛יךָ וְֽרַחֲמֶ֖יךָ אֵלַ֥י הִתְאַפָּֽקוּ׃
records.gloss: Look from heaven and see from [the] lofty dwelling of your holiness and your splendor. Where [are] your zeal and your mighty deeds? [The] stirring of your inward parts and your compassions toward me have restrained themselves.
pieces: Look down from the heavens; \q see from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} exalted dwelling, holy and splendid! \q What has become of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} zeal and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} mighty acts? \q Your tender feeling and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} compassion hold themselves back from me.

L.15: Look from heaven and see, \q from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} lofty dwelling of holiness and splendor! \q Where [are] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} zeal and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} mighty deeds? \q The stirring of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} inner parts and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} compassion are held back toward me.

R.15: Look down from heaven and see us. \q Look from the holy and beautiful place where {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} live. \q Where is {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} burning love for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people? Where are the mighty things {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} used to do? \q Your deep love and kindness are kept away from me.

decisions.choice: look down from heaven, your holy dwelling: the old prayer of Israel
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 26:15 has the same prayer: "Look down from your holy dwelling, from heaven, and bless your people Israel."

decisions.choice: zeal: God's passionate commitment to his people and his name
decisions.reason: The same word is used of the LORD's zeal in 9:6, 26:11, 42:13 and 59:17, where it moves him to act for his people.

decisions.choice: the stirring of your inner parts: God's deep feeling for his people
decisions.reason: The inner organs were thought of as the seat of feeling (16:11; Jeremiah 31:20, where God's inner parts stir for Ephraim).

decisions.choice: your burning love for your people
decisions.reason: Readable explains zeal as God's strong love for his own, following the meaning decision.

records.source: כִּֽי־אַתָּ֣ה אָבִ֔ינוּ כִּ֤י אַבְרָהָם֙ לֹ֣א יְדָעָ֔נוּ וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֹ֣א יַכִּירָ֑נוּ אַתָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ אָבִ֔ינוּ גֹּאֲלֵ֥נוּ מֵֽעוֹלָ֖ם שְׁמֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: For you [are] our father, for Abraham does not know us, and Israel does not acknowledge us; you, Yahweh, [are] our father; our Redeemer from long ago [is] your name.
pieces: Surely {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are our Father, \q even if Abraham has never heard of us \q and Israel would not claim us as his own. \q You, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, are our Father; \q from ages past {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name has been Our Redeemer.

L.16: For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are] our Father, \q though Abraham does not know us \q and Israel does not acknowledge us; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, [are] our Father; \q Our Redeemer from of old [is] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name.

R.16: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are our Father! \q Abraham does not know who we are. \q Jacob does not recognize us as his children. \q But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, are our Father. \q From long ago {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name has been Our Redeemer, the one who rescues us.

decisions.choice: you are our Father: God addressed as Father
decisions.reason: God is rarely called Father in the Old Testament, and directly addressed so only a few times (64:7; Jeremiah 3:4, 19). He is Father as the one who made and claimed Israel as his son (Deuteronomy 32:6; Exodus 4:22; Malachi 2:10).

decisions.choice: Abraham and Israel: the nation's ancestors, who cannot know or own them now
decisions.reason: Israel here is Jacob, the ancestor. Even if the founders of the nation would not recognize their descendants, God still claims them. The verbs know and acknowledge are used of a father owning his children (Deuteronomy 33:9).

decisions.choice: Redeemer: the near relative who buys back what was lost
decisions.reason: The go'el bought back family land and freed relatives from slavery (Leviticus 25:25, 47-49); God is Israel's Redeemer (41:14; 44:6).

decisions.choice: Jacob
decisions.reason: Readable names Israel the ancestor as Jacob, so the reader does not take it as the nation.

records.source: לָ֣מָּה תַתְעֵ֤נוּ יְהוָה֙ מִדְּרָכֶ֔יךָ תַּקְשִׁ֥יחַ לִבֵּ֖נוּ מִיִּרְאָתֶ֑ךָ שׁ֚וּב לְמַ֣עַן עֲבָדֶ֔יךָ שִׁבְטֵ֖י נַחֲלָתֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Why do you make us wander, Yahweh, from your ways, [why] do you harden our heart from fear of you? Return for [the] sake of your servants, [the] tribes of your inheritance.
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} send us straying from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} paths, \q and make our hearts so hard that we no longer fear {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}? \q Turn back to us for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants, \q the tribes that belong to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

L.17: Why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} make us wander, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ways, \q [and] harden our heart from fearing {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}? \q Return for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants, \q the tribes of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} inheritance.

R.17: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} make us wander away from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ways? \q Why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} make us so stubborn that we do not respect {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}? \q Come back to us. Do it for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants, the tribes of Israel that belong to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: you make us wander, you harden our heart: God has left them to their stubbornness as a judgment
decisions.reason: The prayer speaks of God as the cause of their straying, as in 6:9-10 and 29:10, where hardening is God's judgment on those who refused him. It is a cry for him to stop, not an excuse: the people confess their sin in 64:4-6.

decisions.choice: return: turn back to us in favor
decisions.reason: The same plea is in Psalm 90:13: "Return, LORD! How long?"

decisions.choice: the tribes of your inheritance: Israel as God's own portion
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 32:9 says the LORD's portion is his people; Psalm 74:2 makes the same plea.

decisions.choice: Come back to us; the tribes of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says to whom God should return and which tribes are meant.

records.source: לַמִּצְעָ֕ר יָרְשׁ֖וּ עַם־קָדְשֶׁ֑ךָ צָרֵ֕ינוּ בּוֹסְס֖וּ מִקְדָּשֶֽׁךָ׃
records.gloss: For a little [while] they possessed, [the] people of your holiness; our adversaries have trampled your sanctuary.
pieces: Your holy people held the land only a short time; \q now our enemies have trampled {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sanctuary.

L.18: For a little [while] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy people possessed [it]; \q our adversaries have trampled {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sanctuary.

R.18: Your holy people lived in the land for only a short time. \q Now our enemies have stomped all over {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} Temple.

decisions.choice: your holy people possessed the land for a little while
alternatives: for a little while they possessed your holy people
your holy people possessed your holy place for a little while
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated object. The land is the most likely: Israel held it for a short time before enemies took it. The words could also mean that enemies possessed God's holy people for a little while. The line is hard, and the sense is uncertain.

decisions.choice: our adversaries have trampled your sanctuary: the destruction of the temple
decisions.reason: The Babylonians burned the temple in 587 BC (2 Kings 25:9). 64:10 and Psalm 74:3-7 lament the same loss.

decisions.choice: it; the land
decisions.reason: The object is supplied from the meaning decision; Literal brackets it.

records.source: הָיִ֗ינוּ מֵֽעוֹלָם֙ לֹֽא־מָשַׁ֣לְתָּ בָּ֔ם לֹֽא־נִקְרָ֥א שִׁמְךָ֖ עֲלֵיהֶ֑םלוּא־קָרַ֤עְתָּ שָׁמַ֨יִם֙ יָרַ֔דְתָּ מִפָּנֶ֖יךָ הָרִ֥ים נָזֹֽלּוּ׃
records.gloss: We have become from long ago [those] not you have ruled over them, not has been called your name on them. Oh that you would tear [the] heavens, [that] you would come down, [that] from before you [the] mountains would quake.
pieces: For a long time now we have been like a people never under {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} rule, \q a people that never bore {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name. \q If only {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} would split the heavens apart and come down, \q and the mountains would shake as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} came near!

L.19: We have become [like those] whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have not ruled over from long ago, \q [like those] over whom {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name has not been called. \q Oh that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} would tear open the heavens [and] come down, \q [that] the mountains would quake before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}!

R.19: For a long time we have been like people {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} never ruled, \q like people who do not belong to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q Oh, how we wish {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} would tear open the sky and come down! \q The mountains would shake in front of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: verse numbering: the Hebrew text counts "Oh that you would tear open the heavens" as the end of 63:19
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew text this line closes chapter 63. Another common numbering, found in many printed Bibles, makes it 64:1, so that 64:1-11 here are 64:2-12 there. The sense is the same: the line begins the plea that runs on into chapter 64. This translation follows the Hebrew numbers.

decisions.choice: we have become like those you never ruled, those not called by your name
alternatives: we have been yours from long ago; you have not ruled them
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is terse, with no word for "like". Read as a comparison, the people say they have become like the nations that never belonged to God. It could also be read "We have been yours from long ago; you have not ruled them [our enemies], your name was not called over them." To have God's name called over someone means they belong to him (Deuteronomy 28:10; Jeremiah 14:9).

decisions.choice: tear open the heavens and come down: God's coming as at Sinai
decisions.reason: When God came down on Sinai the mountain shook (Exodus 19:18; Judges 5:5; Psalm 18:10). Mark 1:10 uses the picture of the heavens torn open at Jesus' baptism.

decisions.choice: people who do not belong to you
decisions.reason: Readable says what having God's name called over them means.
